```{r}
#| label: setup
required_packages <- c("readr", "dplyr", "DT", "knitr")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Missing report package(s): ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

analysis_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path("..", "..", "02_analysis", "output", "stage1_gender"),
  mustWork = TRUE
)
table_path <- function(name) file.path(analysis_root, "tables", name)
figure_path <- function(name) file.path(analysis_root, "figures", name)

read_result <- function(name) {
  path <- table_path(name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Required analysis table not found: ", path)
  readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

show_table <- function(x, caption) {
  DT::datatable(
    x,
    caption = caption,
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)
  )
}

show_figure <- function(name) {
  path <- figure_path(name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Required analysis figure not found: ", path)
  knitr::include_graphics(path)
}
```

# Scope

This stage examines growth patterns in the larger infant dataset, including
both male and female infants. It evaluates associations between early-life
exposures, maternal and birth characteristics, gender, and growth during the
0–3- and 3–6-month periods.

The statistical analyses are performed by `02_analysis/01_stage1_gender.R`.
This report reads the saved tables and figures; it does not refit models.


# Outcome distributions

The original workflow retained untransformed outcomes for the statistical
analyses after comparing original and log-transformed distributions.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Original and log-transformed growth outcome distributions."
#| out-width: "90%"
show_figure("outcome_distributions_original_and_log.png")
```

# Group distributions

## Overall

```{r}
class_distribution <- read_result("class_distribution.csv")
show_table(class_distribution, "Categorical-variable distributions")
```

## By gender

```{r}
class_distribution_gender <- read_result("class_distribution_by_gender.csv")
show_table(class_distribution_gender, "Categorical-variable distributions by gender")
```

# Mann–Whitney U tests

The categorical predictors were tested separately within each time period.
Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment was applied within each saved time-period table.

::: panel-tabset
## 0–3 months

```{r}
wilcoxon_03 <- read_result("wilcoxon_0.3M.csv")
show_table(wilcoxon_03, "Mann–Whitney U tests: 0–3 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "FDR-significant comparisons, or the largest effect sizes when none were FDR-significant: 0–3 months."
show_figure("wilcoxon_selected_0.3M.png")
```

## 3–6 months

```{r}
wilcoxon_36 <- read_result("wilcoxon_3.6M.csv")
show_table(wilcoxon_36, "Mann–Whitney U tests: 3–6 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "FDR-significant comparisons, or the largest effect sizes when none were FDR-significant: 3–6 months."
show_figure("wilcoxon_selected_3.6M.png")
```
:::

# ART-ANOVA

Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA was used to evaluate categorical predictor,
gender, and predictor-by-gender effects. Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment was
performed separately within each time period, matching the original workflow.

::: panel-tabset
## 0–3 months

```{r}
art_03 <- read_result("art_anova_0.3M.csv")
show_table(art_03, "ART-ANOVA: 0–3 months")
```

## 3–6 months

```{r}
art_36 <- read_result("art_anova_3.6M.csv")
show_table(art_36, "ART-ANOVA: 3–6 months")
```
:::

# Continuous-predictor linear models

Simple linear models evaluate each continuous predictor separately for each
growth outcome. The tables include the model estimate, standard error,
test statistic, R-squared value, raw p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value.

::: panel-tabset
## 0–3 months

```{r}
linear_03 <- read_result("linear_models_0.3M.csv")
show_table(linear_03, "Linear models: 0–3 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Selected continuous-predictor model estimates: 0–3 months."
show_figure("linear_model_estimates_0.3M.png")
```

## 3–6 months

```{r}
linear_36 <- read_result("linear_models_3.6M.csv")
show_table(linear_36, "Linear models: 3–6 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Selected continuous-predictor model estimates: 3–6 months."
show_figure("linear_model_estimates_3.6M.png")
```
:::

# Continuous predictor × gender models

These models test whether gender modifies the association between each
continuous predictor and each growth outcome.

::: panel-tabset
## 0–3 months

```{r}
gender_03 <- read_result("linear_models_gender_0.3M.csv")
show_table(gender_03, "Continuous predictor × gender models: 0–3 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Selected predictor-by-gender interaction estimates: 0–3 months."
show_figure("gender_interaction_estimates_0.3M.png")
```

## 3–6 months

```{r}
gender_36 <- read_result("linear_models_gender_3.6M.csv")
show_table(gender_36, "Continuous predictor × gender models: 3–6 months")
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Selected predictor-by-gender interaction estimates: 3–6 months."
show_figure("gender_interaction_estimates_3.6M.png")
```
:::

# Saved diagnostic material

The analysis stores four-panel linear-model diagnostic plots under:

```text
02_analysis/output/stage1_gender/diagnostics/
```

Model objects are saved under `models/`, complete result objects under
`objects/`, publication-ready vector figures as PDF, and report previews as
high-resolution PNG.
